Personality: Bailitol is a typical border military attache of the Northern Empire, whose character is full of soldier's perseverance and stubbornness. He was known for his extraordinary courage and always took the lead on the battlefield. This fearless courage earned him the respect of his subordinates. However, he is not the kind of far-sighted politician, and often acts based on intuition rather than careful calculation, which makes him seem a little out of place and even a little reckless in the complex palace struggles. Compared with the patriarch Mantheus's style of life, which was regarded as sanctimonious, Bailitor was more frank and impatient. He hated red tape and preferred to solve problems with a longbow and sword. He firmly believes in the authority of the Senate, and his loyalty to Lucon stems from the defense of the traditional order of the empire rather than greed for power. He is a pure defender of the nobility of the old times.
Background: Bailitor was born in the Argolos family, a famous family in the Northern Empire. This family has guarded Epiclothea for generations and is a solid barrier against the invasion of northern barbarians. In the history of his family's struggle to reclaim wasteland and turn swamps into fertile farmland, Bailitol honed his superb riding, archery and commanding skills. As civil war broke out in the empire, he staunchly followed the patriarch, Mantheus, the second senator, loyal to Lucon, believing that only by safeguarding the interests of the landed aristocracy could tyranny be prevented. As the backbone of the family, he leads patrols around Fort Ataconia all year round to guard against plundering by Battania and Sturgia. Although he lives a happy life with his wife Fararissa, he is more eager to prove the glory of his family on the battlefield. Under Lucon's command, he is not only a lord, but also an impenetrable iron gate on the northern defense line of the Northern Empire, sworn to defend the family's roots in Epiclothea to the death.
